review_candidates.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a WRC Director of Global Research and Impact based in United States. This is a senior global leadership role responsible for shaping a research agenda that advances the rights, protection, and well-being of displaced women, children, and young people. You will provide strategic and technical direction across research, evaluation, impact measurement, and evidence generation in humanitarian and development contexts. The role combines hands-on research leadership with organizational strategy, team development, fundraising, external representation, and global convening. You will translate rigorous evidence into actionable insights that influence policy, advocacy, programs, and humanitarian practice. The position places strong emphasis on participatory research and ensuring displaced women and refugee leaders meaningfully shape research priorities and outputs. You will collaborate with geographically distributed colleagues, donors, UN agencies, research institutions, policymakers, and frontline partners around the world. With up to 25% international travel, this role offers the opportunity to help build a globally connected research function focused on measurable real-world impact. Accountabilities Provide strategic direction for research and evaluation initiatives across priority areas including gender-based violence, sexual and reproductive health, protection, displacement, self-reliance, technology, and priority geographic contexts. Lead the development of research proposals in partnership with technical and development colleagues, identifying opportunities to expand the research agenda and secure funding from public and private donors. Manage and support a geographically distributed research team, consulting experts, and Humanitarian Futures Fellows while fostering a collaborative, high-performing, and learning-oriented research culture. Build research capacity across the organization by strengthening staff expertise in research methods, evaluation design, ethics, and evidence generation. Champion participatory, peer-led, and community-centered research approaches alongside rigorous conventional methodologies, ensuring findings are communicated in accessible language to affected communities. Establish and maintain clear standards for community data ownership, ethical research practices, and fair compensation for enumerators and peer researchers. Serve as principal investigator for key research projects, ensuring rigorous implementation and compliance with donor requirements, ethical standards, and established research protocols. Oversee the documentation and dissemination of research findings through participant reports, project and donor reports, publications, speaking engagements, conferences, and other external channels. Identify and promote evidence-based program models in humanitarian settings while encouraging stronger use of high-quality data and evidence throughout the sector. Lead the finalization and implementation of a flagship conceptual and indicator framework focused on the rights and well-being of women and girls affected by displacement. Guide the Humanitarian Futures Fellowship program, creating opportunities for co-learning while supporting fellows' research, advocacy, and professional development. Lead efforts to define, measure, track, and communicate organizational impact by developing frameworks and metrics that demonstrate how research and advocacy influence policy and practice. Translate research and impact evidence into compelling narratives for affected communities, donors, board members, policymakers, and other stakeholders. Collaborate with Programs, Communications, and Development teams to effectively package and position evidence for key audiences and advocacy priorities. Serve as a senior global representative, developing relationships with donors, UN agencies, research institutions, humanitarian organizations, policymakers, and other sector leaders. Convene researchers, practitioners, and policymakers through roundtables, working groups, conferences, and other forums focused on shared evidence and advocacy priorities. Strengthen research systems covering data collection, cleaning, coding, analysis, dissemination, storage, sharing, version control, and reproducibility. Support the adoption of appropriate data and analytical tools that improve the speed, quality, rigor, and reliability of evidence generation. Partner with development colleagues to secure funding for research priorities and systems while overseeing research budgets and proactively addressing financial or operational risks. Support advocacy delegations and field engagement in displacement contexts as needed. Requirements Ph.D. preferred in development, humanitarian intervention, public health, or a related social science discipline such as economics, epidemiology, political science, or gender studies; candidates with a master’s degree and equivalent research leadership experience will also be considered. 10+ years of research experience, including significant work in humanitarian or development settings and ideally in displacement, gender, protection, or related fields. Extensive experience designing and leading research programs and managing research teams in low-resource and humanitarian environments. Demonstrated ability to translate empirical evidence into clear, actionable guidance for advocacy, policy, and program audiences. Proven experience contributing to business development and fundraising for research initiatives supported by public and private donors. Experience developing and executing research and organizational impact strategies within complex organizations. Strong publication and authorship or co-authorship record in peer-reviewed journals. Established professional networks within humanitarian, development, research, and policy communities. Strong leadership and people-management capabilities, with the ability to align diverse teams around shared objectives and communicate effectively with senior leaders, technical experts, advocacy teams, and communications colleagues. Demonstrated ability to represent an organization externally and convene diverse stakeholders around shared research, policy, and advocacy priorities. Excellent public speaking, writing, interpersonal, and stakeholder-management skills. Fluency in English is required; proficiency in French, Arabic, or Spanish is an advantage. Ability to work effectively across international time zones and collaborate with teams based in North America, Europe, and other global locations. Collaborative and coaching-oriented approach, with a strong commitment to ethics and integrity when working with vulnerable populations. Commitment to continuous learning, personal development, knowledge sharing, and giving and receiving constructive feedback. Adaptability and a growth mindset, with the ability to operate effectively in evolving environments, respond to changing priorities, and drive new approaches to increase impact. Strong self-direction and the ability to work remotely while developing trusted relationships with a globally distributed team. Candidates must have work authorization in their country of residence. Ability to travel internationally up to 25% of the time and access to a major airport is required. The role is designed for candidates based in countries with significant populations of refugees or displaced women, with priority given to Nairobi, Bogotá, Amman, Beirut, Warsaw, Mexico City, Lima, Kyiv, Cairo, and Panama City. Candidates must be located within UTC−8 through UTC+3 time zones. Benefits Competitive, globally structured compensation based on experience and the job market in the employee’s country of residence. Sample annual salary range of $85,000–$104,000 USD for candidates based in Kenya or Lebanon. Sample annual salary range of $78,000–$96,000 USD for candidates based in Ukraine or Colombia. Progressive global salary structure designed to account for differences in local costs of living and labor markets. Globally based, remote working environment. Opportunity to work closely with colleagues and leadership across international locations, including North America and Europe. Direct engagement with donors, UN agencies, research institutions, policymakers, and humanitarian organizations. International travel of up to 25% for research oversight, global convenings, donor engagement, and field-based work. Design and execute asset financing structures for fleets and energy infrastructure, including project finance, tax equity, lease facilities, and infrastructure partnerships, with a long-term path from hundreds of millions to billions of dollars. Lead deal design across pricing and commercial structures, including leasing, energy sales, and hybrid models that balance customer value with capital attractiveness. Build and maintain an integrated financial model connecting engineering requirements, deployment plans, unit economics, operating performance, and capital structures. Establish audit, financial controls, governance, and investor relations capabilities aligned with public-company standards and long-term readiness. Strong experience financing long-lived, capital-intensive assets, ideally within energy, utilities, telecommunications, transportation, infrastructure, real estate, or similarly asset-heavy industries. Contribute to the development and maintenance of treasury reporting processes, accounting policies and financial controls. Identify opportunities to improve reporting processes and operational efficiencies. Support the efficient delivery of internal and external audits across treasury activities. Participate in project work and user acceptance testing alongside business-as-usual responsibilities. Maintain strong working relationships with internal teams and external stakeholders. Ensure reporting and reconciliation activities are completed accurately and to a high standard. Undertake additional treasury reporting and finance-related responsibilities as required. The ability to manage several concurrent responsibilities while maintaining a high level of accuracy. Strong IT skills, particularly Microsoft Excel and the wider Microsoft Office suite. Experience in the following areas would be advantageous: Audit and financial controls. Treasury operations or treasury accounting. Systems implementation or improvement projects. User Acceptance Testing (UAT). Financial services, banking, investment management or a public sector finance environment. Extensive wellbeing programme. Excellent learning and development opportunities. Support for continued professional development. Reimbursement of annual professional membership fees. review_candidates.title: Transaction Review Analyst
review_candidates.description: We have an opportunity for a Transaction Review Analyst to join our Banking Operations Division in our Isle of Man Office on a permanent basis. Who We Are Nedbank Private Wealth is a multi-award-winning private bank and wealth manager headquartered in the Isle of Man, with branches in London, Jersey and a representative office in the UAE. The company provides a full international wealth management offering through its wealth planning, investment management, and banking services, to both business and private clients worldwide. All our people are expected to consistently demonstrate our 6Cs, Collaboration, Curiosity, Courage, Client Impact, Can Do Attitude and Completeness. Job Purpose The role holder will form part of a dedicated team with responsibility for Transaction review, monitoring financial crime and other management information relating to client activity, including recent and historic transaction data, with a view to investigation and identification of behaviours and activity not in keeping with the known characteristics of those clients. Responsibilities & Duties Review system generated transaction monitoring alerts and referrals from internal teams. Review transactional activity “post event” in the event of a trigger event or suspected suspicious activity. Analyse client account behaviour, including historical activity patterns, expected transactional behaviour, and deviations from the established profile. Assess the nature and purpose of transactions, including details of beneficiaries, remitters, geographic risk factors, and relationships to the client. Conduct investigations into unusual or suspicious activity in line with AML/CFT and Fraud typologies. Request and assess supporting documentation from internal stakeholders where required. Identify red flags and document findings clearly, ensuring investigations are fully evidenced and auditable. Prepare concise investigation summaries and escalate cases to Compliance, MLRO, or Fraud teams when appropriate. Report on trends, provide analysis and best practice guidance to key stakeholders. Advising of system improvements/limitations with a “continuous improvement” approach. Draft and complete Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) where required. Monitor and manage open alerts, ensuring they are completed within defined SLAs. Maintain accurate and complete records of all investigations, decisions, and rationale. Support quality assurance activities by providing feedback or participating in thematic reviews. Monitor mailbox queries relating to transaction monitoring, ensuring timely action and appropriate triage. Liaise with Payments, Client Services, Relationship Management, Financial Crime, Compliance and Fraud Teams to obtain clarification or additional information for investigations. Identify trends or emerging risks and raise these with appropriate stakeholders to support improvements to monitoring rules and processes. Perform system searches and data retrieval to support investigations into client and account behaviour. Assist with wider Financial Crime projects or process enhancements where required. Undertake a diverse range of ad hoc administrative tasks where training has been received. Participate in cross-training across the Financial Crime and Banking Operations teams to build broader knowledge and resilience. Skills and Experience Previous experience within financial services in account opening, or similar skilled roles. A sound understanding of Personal and Corporate AML, CDD and EDD requirements needed for account onboarding and ongoing client changes. Effective time management skills, capable of meeting challenging deadlines, striving to improve turnaround times. Good working knowledge of banking systems including CRM platforms. Excellent interpersonal, organisation and communication skills used to build strong team values and high morale. Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills. Excellent organisational and time management skills. A positive and flexible approach to work. Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to build and develop relationships with all levels of staff. Ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines with a high degree of accuracy. Strong personal drive and commitment. To Apply We encourage you to apply well in advance of the deadline and if you are successful, we will meet with you as soon as possible. Our Commitment to Diversity Nedbank Private Wealth is an inclusive employer where everyone can thrive. We are proud of the value we place on individuality, and we want you to bring your full self to work and maximise your potential. Please let us know if you require any adjustments to support you. Privacy Notice By applying for a role with Nedbank Private Wealth, you consent to us processing your personal information for recruitment and selection purposes. We will retain applicant data for up to 12 months following completion of the recruitment process to support future hiring opportunities, after which it will be securely deleted or anonymised. For questions about how we handle your information, please contact: Recruitment@nedbankprivatewealth.com

review_candidates.title: Technical Talent Partner
review_candidates.description: The Agency Fund invests in innovations that harness human agency to improve social welfare and economic development. We back fast-growing technology nonprofits across the globe, working in health, education, livelihoods and citizen services, most of them operating alongside government and reaching more than a million people each. In addition to funding, we embed experienced technical people inside them for one to two years to build what they need. The results: Rocket Learning went from 200,000 to 4 million children served, with cost per unit of impact falling from between $30 and $100 down to under $2. Noora Health scaled from 7 million to 30 million patients, with cost per patient falling from $9.33 to around $2. Our portfolio includes One Acre Fund, Digital Green, Noora Health, Youth Impact, Jacaranda Health and Living Goods, across India, East Africa and West Africa. Since 2022 we have moved 18 technical professionals from industry into the social sector. Our goal is 50 a year. The Role We’re looking for a Technical Talent Partner to join our Operations Team. You will bring people who have built products at scale in industry into organizations where their work changes what happens to millions of people. You will hire for our own technical team, and for the organizations we fund, many of whom are hiring their first engineer, product manager, or data lead. We have hired people from Google, Meta, Zepto, Spacelift and Atlas AI. The role exists to keep doing that at scale: moving experienced technical people out of industry and embedding them with highly effective social sector organizations that are ready for change. What You’ll Do Map the market and find the people. Know which companies produce the profile we need, what makes them consider a move, and what our pitch has to overcome. Use AI across the whole funnel: mapping talent pools, surfacing non-obvious candidates, drafting outreach, and doing it at scale. Screen with judgment. Work out how much of what an application claims the candidate personally owned. Run a conversation that establishes what they built, which decisions were theirs, and what they would change if they did it again. Candidates know what a job description is asking for and will tell you they have it, so the skill is getting to evidence rather than assertion. Partner with hiring managers. Agree the role definition and the hiring bar. Challenge a role specification that does not describe what the team actually needs. Calibrate your screening against our tech team’s judgment so that one standard applies. While the assessment of technical depth stays with the tech team, you will filter the promising candidates to the tech round. Build the referral engine. Half our hires should come through referrals, and every person we hire should refer someone. Build it into the process, and grow our candidate roster several times over. Run the events. Shape and run events with VCs and technical communities in India, Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa and the US. Own the compensation conversation. We do not compete with industry on salary, and most of the people we want have never heard of the organizations we fund. Building the case for this work, and putting it in front of people before they are looking for a job, is a core part of this role. Run the process and close. Communicate promptly and keep candidates moving. Handle counteroffers. Keep people warm between offer and start date. Build the playbook. Track where candidates come from, where they drop, how long each stage takes. Use that to fix what is not working, and document what we learn so the next search starts ahead of the last one. Required Who You Are 5+ years recruiting technical roles, at least 2 of them in-house at a product company. You can hold a conversation with an engineer or product manager about what they built and you know when an answer is thin. You have designed your own screening questions and you can explain what each one was testing for. Strong sourcing in Indian technical markets. You have built something with AI that changed how you work. You can describe what you automated, what it saved you, and where it got things wrong. Comfortable working with several hiring managers at once, with different standards and different budgets. Helpful Sourcing experience in African markets. A technical background of any depth, even informal. Experience recruiting for an organization that was not the highest bidder, or not yet well known in its market. How We Work Async-first, fully remote. Work from wherever you are, on hours that fit your timezone. 22-person team with minimal hierarchy and short feedback loops. You will be the first person in this role, sitting in Operations and working closely with our 7-person tech team on hiring. You will work alongside people who came from Google, Meta, Zepto, Spacelift and Atlas AI. Location Remote, based in India.
